label: Mech-interp circuits are clean, localized subgraphs of the model
description:
Early mech-interp results — induction heads in particular — gave the impression that circuits are clean: a small, identifiable group of attention heads + MLP neurons that implement a single behavior. Find the right heads, ablate them, watch the behavior disappear. Done.

It's rarely that clean. Two structural reasons:

**Superposition.** Models pack more features than dimensions. A single attention head or MLP neuron rarely corresponds to one concept; it carries information about many features that rarely co-occur. When you 'identify a head that does X,' you're often identifying a head where X is *one of several* things it does. Ablating the head removes X *and* a bunch of other capabilities, making the ablation evidence ambiguous.

**Distributed circuits.** Many capabilities are implemented across many heads/layers cooperatively. Ablating any single head only partially degrades the behavior. Identifying 'the circuit' for a capability is harder when the circuit is 5% in head 3.2, 10% in head 5.7, etc., across the model.

This is why **sparse autoencoders (SAEs)** have become the workhorse of modern mech-interp. SAEs decompress the model's activations into a wider, sparser feature space where individual features are more cleanly identifiable. Circuits in feature-space are still distributed, but each feature is more interpretable than the underlying neurons or attention components.

The takeaway: induction heads were a clean find because they happen to be a clean circuit. Most circuits aren't.
probeQuestions: Why does ablating a single attention head rarely cleanly remove a single capability?
What does 'superposition' imply for the interpretability of individual neurons?
correctionPromptTemplate: The learner thinks mech-interp circuits are clean, localized subgraphs. Walk through: superposition means individual neurons / heads carry many features. Most circuits are distributed across many heads and layers, with each head contributing partially. Sparse autoencoders are the modern response — decompress activations into a wider, sparser feature space. Ask first — 'if circuits were always clean, why has the field moved from neuron-level interpretation to sparse-autoencoder feature dictionaries?'
